definitions.explanation: Feeling sympathy for someone in an unfortunate situation.

examples.japanese: {可哀想|かわいそう}な{犬|いぬ}
あの{子|こ}は{可哀想|かわいそう}だ。
{彼|かれ}を{叱|しか}るのは{可哀想|かわいそう}だよ。
examples.notes: [Note: 〜のは可哀想だ = it's cruel/pitiable to ~]

examples.japanese: {病気|びょうき}の{子猫|こねこ}を{見|み}て、{可哀想|かわいそう}で{涙|なみだ}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: Seeing the sick kitten, I felt so sorry that tears came out.

notes:
{可哀想|かわいそう} expresses sympathy or pity.

KANJI VARIATIONS:
- {可哀想|かわいそう}: standard spelling
- {可哀相|かわいそう}: alternate spelling
- かわいそう: hiragana (common)

USAGE PATTERNS:
- {可哀想|かわいそう}な + noun
- 〜は{可哀想|かわいそう}だ
- 〜て{可哀想|かわいそう} (I feel sorry that...)

NOTE: {可愛|かわい}い (cute) and {可哀想|かわいそう} (pitiable) are different words despite similar sounds.
